place.zh: 沉鼎观 · 药园 · 这一年
place.en: Chending Temple · The herb garden · That year

setup.zh: 马小宝押了七回没押着，告到执事房：沈小满送人的丹，九道纹；药园是他巡的。周衡翻开巡夜簿：「药园，一株不少。要告他偷，拿赃来。」
setup.en: Seven bets and not one win; Ma Xiaobao goes to the stewards' office: the pills Shen Xiaoman gives away have nine rings, and he patrols the herb garden. Zhou Heng opens the night-watch book: "The herb garden — not one plant short. If you accuse him of theft, bring the stolen goods."

recap.zh: 马小宝告你偷了药园的灵草，周衡翻开巡夜簿：「药园，一株不少……要告他偷，拿赃来。」又问孙二狗那颗丹几道纹——「我看了」。清明替外公烧了纸；伏天里阿禾吞了那颗丹。一晃五年，祁长松筑了基，第五年腊八你规规矩矩赢了大比，观里那颗一转的官丹，揭了封，米汤粘回去，进了饭桶；入秋，九层大圆满。
recap.en: Ma Xiaobao accused you of stealing from the herb garden; Zhou Heng opened the night-watch book: "The herb garden, not one plant short… if you accuse him of theft, bring the stolen goods." Then he asked how many rings Sun Ergou's pill had — "I looked." At Qingming you burned paper for Grandfather; in the dog days A-He swallowed her pill. Five years went by; Qi Changsong laid his Foundation, and at Laba in the fifth year you won the contest plainly; the temple's one-turn pill, its seal lifted and glued back with rice water, went into the Rice Tub; by autumn, layer nine, great perfection.

en: "The herb garden — not one plant short."
"If you accuse him of theft, bring the stolen goods."

story.zh:
往后残株一个月一篮，篮子一年比一年浅，两三个月才出得一颗。

马小宝去坊市钱掌柜的摊子上一押三十两，押了七回，连一颗一道纹的也没押着。押到第七回，他不押了。他去了执事房。

「周师兄，」他当着一屋子领灵石的人道，「沈小满送人的丹，九道纹。钱掌柜这辈子没开过头彩，这是他自己赌咒说的。一个大比时才四层的，一开春便是五层，还一包一包的丹送人——药园是他巡的。」

这话有人信。一个四层打进了宗门大比的决赛，全观嘀咕了一冬，没人说得清他是怎么打的；如今他又一包一包往外送丹，药园又是他巡的——偷了园里的灵草炼丹，倒比押中头彩说得通。不到天黑，内门的饭堂里也在说这件事了。

周衡没有抬头，把巡夜簿翻开，一页一页往后翻，翻到末了，道：「药园，一株不少。残株是我给的，一个月一篮，账上有。」他合上簿子，看着马小宝：「要告他偷，拿赃来。」马小宝没有赃。他站了一会儿，走了。

人散了，周衡却叫住小满，把账簿往胳膊底下一夹，低声问了一句：「孙二狗那颗聚气丹，几道纹？」

小满道：「他吃得急，没顾上看。」

周衡看着他，道：「我看了。」他没再说什么，走了。往后残株照旧一个月一篮，他再没问过一个字；可每回递篮子，他都要多看小满一眼。
story.en:
After that the culls came one basket a month, the basket shallower every year, and a pill only every two or three months.

Ma Xiaobao went to Shopkeeper Qian's stall in the market and staked thirty taels a time, seven times, and did not win so much as a one-ring pill. After the seventh, he stopped. He went to the stewards' office.

"Brother Zhou," he said, before a roomful of people come for their spirit stones, "the pills Shen Xiaoman gives away have nine rings. Shopkeeper Qian has never paid out a top prize in his life — he swore it himself. Layer four at the contest, layer five come spring, and packet after packet of pills to give away — and he's the one who patrols the herb garden."

People believed it. A layer-four had fought his way into the final of the sect contest, and the whole temple had muttered about it all winter — no one could say how he had fought; now he was handing out pills by the packet, and he was the one who patrolled the herb garden. Stealing the garden's spirit herbs to make pills made better sense than a top prize. Before dark they were talking of it in the inner court's dining hall too.

Zhou Heng didn't look up. He opened the night-watch book and turned it page by page to the end, and said: "The herb garden — not one plant short. The culls I give him, one basket a month; it's in the books." He shut the book and looked at Ma Xiaobao: "If you accuse him of theft, bring the stolen goods." Ma Xiaobao had none. He stood a while, and left.

When the people had gone, Zhou Heng called Xiaoman back, tucked the ledger under his arm, and asked, low: "Sun Ergou's qi pill — how many rings?"

Xiaoman said: "He ate it in a hurry. Didn't stop to look."

Zhou Heng looked at him and said: "I looked." He said nothing more, and left. After that the culls came one basket a month as before, and he never asked another word; but every time he handed over the basket, he gave Xiaoman one look more.

exits.means: the spring: burns paper for his grandfather facing Mengshan; A-He's foot of rice in the herb garden, fed with her own qi

story.zh:
清明那天，他在后山寻了一块向着蒙山的石头，替外公烧了一沓黄纸——外公的坟在镇上，他去不了。他念着他娘教的口诀，念到「五居中央」，纸烧完了，灰飞起来，打着旋儿往山下去。

那天傍晚，他去药园东角寻阿禾。那一尺地是她找周衡租的，一月半块灵石。开春她启了竹筒上的蜡，把禾种倒出来，种了下去，出了二十来棵，一棵一棵地黄。她便夜夜把手按在土上，拿自己的气喂它们。禾不黄了，她自己的修为却慢了：开春二层，入夏才三层。小满蹲在她旁边看了一会儿，没说话。
story.en:
On Qingming he found a rock on the back hill facing Mengshan and burned a stack of yellow paper for Grandfather — Grandfather's grave was in the town, and he could not go. He recited the formula his mother had taught him; as he reached "five in the middle", the paper burned out, and the ash flew up and spun away down the mountain.

That evening he went to find A-He at the east corner of the herb garden. That foot of earth she rented from Zhou Heng at half a spirit stone a month. In spring she broke the wax on her bamboo tube, shook out the rice seed and sowed it; twenty-odd shoots came up, and one by one they yellowed. So every night she pressed her hand to the soil and fed them with her own qi. The rice stopped yellowing, but her own cultivation slowed: layer two in spring, only three by summer. Xiaoman squatted beside her and watched a while, and said nothing.

label.en: The dog days · Five years go by

exits.means: the hot months: nights on the herb-garden wall with A-He and Sun Ergou, A-He's nine-ring pill — then five years in a few lines (layers six to nine; Qi Changsong's Foundation and his first flight into the cypress; the year-five contest won plainly, the sect's one-turn pill resealed with rice water into the Rice Tub; spells by element, the gourd, Old Qu's sword; five brides on the Zhang)

refuse.zh: 一季一季来：先过了前头那一季。
refuse.en: One season at a time: finish the one before first.

story.zh:
伏天里最热的那几夜，药园巡完了，三个人常坐在药园的矮墙上乘凉：小满，阿禾，孙二狗。

小满问：「你想叫什么？」孙二狗想了半天，道：「……还叫二狗吧。我娘叫惯了。」

小满没笑。阿禾也没笑。墙底下的小狰翻了个身，打了个响鼻。

伏天里的一个晌午，阿禾下山挤到钱掌柜的摊子跟前，把半文钱放在秤盘上，道：「问一句话。你这儿，出过九道纹的聚气丹没有？」钱掌柜的手在算盘上停了一停，道：「我这儿只出一道纹。」他看了她一会儿，又道：「姑娘手里要是有九道纹的，我出五十两收。」阿禾道：「不卖。」那天夜里，她蹲在那一尺地头，把那颗丹吞了。天亮的时候，她是练气五层了。她翻开本子，在他那一页上，写了很长很长的一行。

一晃，便是五年。

看官，凡人修仙，最不值钱的是日子。练气头几层，几个月一层；越往上越慢，一层爬上一两年，是常事；从练气到筑基，十年八年算快的，一辈子爬不上去的，十个里倒有九个。一届百来个进山门的，练到九层大圆满的，不过三五个。

沈小满这五年，说书的只消几行。他一年一层：六层，七层，八层，九层；七层上卡了大半年，他也不急。秘境里那一撮土，在他丹田里长成了一块厚地，吸一口，存一口，一滴不漏；饭桶吐出一颗九道纹的，他吃一颗，那口缸便深一截。夜里他坐着吐纳，木牌贴在心口，凉的时候多，暖的时候少；可他知道，他睡着以后，有一只爪子还在他身子里，一下一下地凿。

五年里，他一回也没回过石坳村。瞿老不许：「没筑基，别下山。」又道：「在你家门口站过一夜的那个人，等的就是你下山。」家信一年两封，他娘的字仍旧又小又密：屋顶不漏了；你爹的膝盖，阴天疼，晴天也疼；吴婆婆的牙，还在。

内门的屋子，一间也没空出来——内门的人筑不了基，又不肯下山，屋子便不空。他仍旧睡在大通铺最靠门的那张铺上，巡夜令挂在腰里，园里一株也没少过。大比年年比，那一颗筑基丹，年年是内门的；头几年，他不上台——那颗丹，九层大圆满才吃得，他五层、六层、七层，拿了也只能揣着，倒招一观的眼睛。祁长松转过年开春便出了关，筑了基，一转的丹，十个里冲得过三四个，他是那三四个里的一个；观里改口叫他祁师叔，他头一回踩着剑从后山飞下来，飞得不稳，一头落在演武场东角那棵老柏上。第五年腊八，小满九层了，才又上了一回五行台。这一回没有猪蜻蜓，也没有镜子，五场，一场一场打下来，打得规规矩矩，台下的人都说没意思。周衡把那本蓝布面的名录翻到新的一页，提起笔来，写了「沈小满」三个字，笔停了一停——三百年的名录上，头一回写一个五门伪灵根的名字。观主把玉盒子放在他手里，封条上盖着大印。当夜他在柴房里揭了封条，盒盖一开，一股药气又苦又腥；一道纹，纹边两三点黑斑，一转，下品；饭桶闻了一口，满脸嫌弃，炉盖一合，再不理他。他讨了半碗米汤，把封条粘了回去，连玉盒子塞进饭桶肚里——全天下唯一一颗他拿出来说得清来历的筑基丹。这几年他学的，也不只是层数：褚先生讲堂上那几样五行的法术，别人一门灵根练一样，他五门都开着，金木水火土挨个儿练了个遍；邹青松那只赤铜葫芦，他夜里关起柴房的门，拿自己的火气一丝一丝喂；瞿老那把扫帚，一个月两回，在崖顶上教他巽四的剑。秦雁第二年进了内门，第五年上，筑了基。孙二狗两年一层，爬到了三层，爬上一层，便在大通铺门口哭一回。阿禾那一尺地年年种，年年多半是瘪穗；她的修为跟着那几棵禾，一年只挪一点。钱掌柜年年腊月把板子扛上山，年年见了小满，头一句话都是：「你那张弓的木头，打听出名字没有？」

每年除夕，周衡都要去一趟正殿；每年从正殿出来，都说一句：「明年，弟子再来。」观主每年都是那一句：外门里，今年没人筑基。每年十月十八，周衡一整天不翻账簿，巡夜的蜡烛，也不掰了。小满不问。

这五年，漳水边上，每年十月十八，推下去一只船，船上坐一个穿嫁衣的姑娘。五年，五只船。沉鼎观离漳水十天的路，观里没有一个人知道她们叫什么。周衡知道是哪一天。
story.en:
On the hottest nights of the dog days, when the garden round was done, the three of them would sit on the herb garden's low wall to cool off: Xiaoman, A-He, Sun Ergou.

Xiaoman asked: "What would you like to be called?" Sun Ergou thought for a long time and said: "…Ergou still. My mother's used to it."

Xiaoman did not laugh. Nor did A-He. Under the wall the little Zheng rolled over and snorted.

One noon in the dog days A-He went down the mountain, squeezed up to Shopkeeper Qian's stall, put half a cash on the scale pan, and said: "One question. Has anything from this stall ever come out as a nine-ring qi pill?" Shopkeeper Qian's hand stopped on the abacus. "My stall only gives one ring." He looked at her a while, and added: "If the young lady has a nine-ring one in hand, I'll pay fifty taels for it." "Not for sale," said A-He. That night she squatted at the head of her foot of earth and swallowed the pill. By dawn she was at Qi Refining layer five. She opened her notebook, and on his page she wrote a very, very long line.

Five years went by in a blink.

Reader, in mortal cultivation days are the cheapest thing there is. The first few layers of Qi Refining take a few months each; the higher you climb the slower it goes, a year or two for a single layer is common; from Qi Refining to Foundation, eight or ten years counts as fast, and nine in ten never make it in a lifetime. Of the hundred-odd who come through the gate in one intake, three or five reach layer nine, great perfection.

Shen Xiaoman's five years the storyteller can tell in a few lines. One layer a year: six, seven, eight, nine; he was stuck at seven for most of a year and did not fret. The pinch of earth from the secret realm had grown into a field of thick soil in his dantian: one breath in, one breath kept, not a drop leaking. Each nine-ring pill the Rice Tub gave up, he ate, and each one made the jar a little deeper. At night he sat breathing, the token against his heart, cool more often than warm; but he knew that once he slept, a claw was still at work inside him, chipping, stroke by stroke.

In five years he never once went back to Shi'ao Village. Old Qu would not allow it: "No Foundation, no going down the mountain." And: "The man who stood a night at your door is waiting for exactly that." Letters came twice a year, his mother's hand still small and dense: the roof doesn't leak now; your father's knee hurts when it's overcast, and when it's clear too; Granny Wu's teeth are still there.

Not one inner-court room came free — inner-court people who couldn't lay their Foundation wouldn't go down the mountain either, so the rooms never emptied. He still slept in the bunk nearest the door, the night-watch token at his belt, and not one plant went missing from the garden. The contest came round every year, and every year the one Foundation pill went to the inner court; the first few years he didn't go up — the pill was for layer nine, great perfection; at five, six, seven he could only have carried it about, and drawn the whole temple's eyes. Qi Changsong came out of seclusion the very next spring and laid his Foundation: on a one-turn pill three or four in ten get through, and he was one of the three or four; the temple took to calling him Uncle-Master Qi, and the first time he flew down from the back mountain on a sword he flew unsteadily and came down headfirst in the old cypress at the east corner of the training ground. At Laba in the fifth year, at layer nine, Xiaoman went up on the Five Elements Platform once more. This time there was no pig-copter and no mirror: five bouts, fought one after another, by the rules, and the crowd below all said it was dull. Zhou Heng turned the blue register to a new page, took up his brush, and wrote the three characters Shen Xiaoman, and the brush paused — in three hundred years of the register, the first time it held the name of a five-door false root. The abbot laid the jade box in his hands, the seal stamped with the great seal. That night in the woodshed he lifted the seal; the lid opened on a smell both bitter and rank: one ring, two or three dark flecks beside it, one-turn, low grade; the Rice Tub sniffed it once, pulled a face of disgust, shut its lid, and would have nothing more to do with him. He begged half a bowl of rice water, glued the seal back down, and tucked it, jade box and all, into the Rice Tub's belly — the one Foundation pill in all the world whose history he could tell. Nor was it only layers he learned in those years: the few five-element spells from Master Chu's lecture hall, where others trained one for their one root, he with all five doors open worked through metal, wood, water, fire and earth in turn; Zou Qingsong's red-copper gourd he fed, nights, behind the barred woodshed door, with his own fire, wisp by wisp; and Old Qu's broom, twice a month on the clifftop, taught him the sword of Xun Four. Qin Yan entered the inner court the next year, and in the fifth year she laid her Foundation. Sun Ergou climbed a layer every two years, up to three, and every layer he climbed he cried once at the door of the long bunk. A-He sowed her foot of earth every year, and every year most of the ears were empty; her cultivation followed those few stalks, moving only a little each year. Every twelfth month Shopkeeper Qian carried his board up the mountain, and every year, seeing Xiaoman, the first thing he said was: "The wood of that bow of yours — found out its name yet?"

Every New Year's Eve, Zhou Heng went to the main hall; every year he came out and said, "Next year I'll come again." Every year the abbot said the same thing: nobody in the outer court has laid a Foundation this year. Every year on the eighteenth of the tenth month Zhou Heng did not open his ledger all day, and did not break his night-watch candle in half. Xiaoman did not ask.

In those five years, every eighteenth of the tenth month, a boat was pushed out on the Zhang with a girl in a bridal gown sitting in it. Five years, five boats. Chending Temple was ten days from the Zhang, and no one in it knew their names. Zhou Heng knew which day it was.

exits.means: the autumn month: the lake brims over, layer nine, great perfection; his master calls him up the cliff

story.zh:
到得入秋，丹田里那口水缸满得往外直漾，吸进去一口灵气，便溢出来一口，再也添不进去了——外门的人管这个叫「九层巅峰」；褚先生的名册上，只写四个字：九层大圆满。

八月里，瞿老叫他上了一趟崖顶。
story.en:
By autumn the great jar in his dantian was brimming over: breathe in one breath of spirit and one spilled out; nothing more would go in — the outer court called this "the peak of layer nine"; in Master Chu's register it was written in four characters only: layer nine, great perfection.

In the eighth month, Old Qu called him up to the clifftop.
